nodes.label: User as Engram: Internalizing Per-User Memory as Local Parametric Edits
nodes.author: Bojie Li, Pine AI
nodes.rationale: Core contribution: splits personal memory into content (per-user facts as local Engram-row overrides) and reasoning skill (shared LoRA adapter). Achieves 33,000× smaller memory footprint than per-user LoRA and 5.6× higher indirect-reasoning accuracy.

nodes.label: Engram Architecture
nodes.author: Cheng et al., 2026
nodes.rationale: Conditional memory form of sparsity complementing MoE; uses suffix N-gram hashing into prime-sized embedding tables with gated lookups; deterministic addressing enables DRAM offloading.

nodes.label: Mini-Engram Models (178M-1.22B)
nodes.author: Bojie Li
nodes.rationale: Four public replications of Engram at nano scale: d8 (178M), d12 (339M), d12@1280 (625M), d20@1536 (1.22B); trained on single Blackwell GPU; released with code and data.

nodes.label: Per-User LoRA Adapter
nodes.author: Hu et al., 2022
nodes.rationale: Standard recipe for in-weights personalization; global weight delta causes contamination on unrelated text (+1.784 bpb vs +0.00005 for Engram row); lacks reasoning skill for indirect questions.

nodes.label: LOCOMO Benchmark
nodes.author: Maharana et al., 2024
nodes.rationale: Long-term conversational memory benchmark; User-as-Engram Joint OPT clears retrieval baselines on single-hop token-F1; enables per-question evidence pointers for apples-to-apples comparison.

nodes.label: Engram Surgical Row Insertion
nodes.rationale: Three strategies for writing facts: UNEMBED_P (closed form, <1ms), OPT (gradient steps, ~1s), Joint OPT (all rows together, default for ≥30 facts/user). Result is ~88KB per-user override map.

nodes.label: Layered Architecture: Per-User Content + Shared Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Splits memory into per-user Engram rows (content) and one shared LoRA (reasoning skill); matches per-user LoRA on direct recall (100% vs 99%) while delivering 7.4× indirect_any (44% vs 6%); zero contamination on unrelated text.

nodes.label: EngramServer Multi-Tenant System
nodes.rationale: ~50-line wrapper for multi-tenant serving; per-request work independent of user count; 232 req/s throughput at 30u/50f, holds 226 req/s at 100u/100f; zero cross-user leakage by design.

nodes.label: Complementary Learning Systems Theory
nodes.author: McClelland et al., 1995; Kumaran et al., 2016
nodes.rationale: Biological inspiration: hippocampal engrams (fast, sparse, local) separate from neocortex (slow, distributed skills); User-as-Engram mirrors this split architecturally to avoid catastrophic interference.

nodes.label: RAG vs Engram Trade-offs
nodes.rationale: Layered design invariant to KB size; RAG degrades as candidates grow; crossover at ~100 facts where Engram decisively wins; different failure modes: Engram density ceiling (per-user facts), RAG retrieval ceiling (candidate pool).

nodes.label: Multi-Hop Reasoning Limitation
nodes.rationale: Engram matches surface N-grams but does not compose facts; when query ends in second fact's words: 90.6% recall; true chaining required: 12.9% recall. Inherited from per-user LoRA architecture.

nodes.label: Within-User Fact Density Ceiling
nodes.rationale: Joint OPT tracks LoRA rank-64 to within few top-5 points at 300 facts/user; at 1000 facts reaches 35% top-1. Constraint is forward-pass interference among co-active rows, not hash collisions; slot space <1% occupied.

nodes.label: Storage Cost Comparison
nodes.rationale: User-as-Engram: ~88KB at 100 facts/user, ~0.9KB/fact; per-user LoRA: 14.2MB fact-count-independent; 161× larger at 100 facts, 1700× at 10 facts; at 1M users: 100GB vs 14.2TB.

nodes.label: Paraphrase Generalization via Multi-Trigger Insertion
nodes.rationale: Single-trigger: 68% top-1 on exact queries, misses paraphrases; multi-trigger insertion: 96.9% top-1 on paraphrases vs 75% for retrieval; explicit contract (trigger N-gram) vs encoder similarity.

nodes.label: Per-User LoRA Contamination Measurement
nodes.rationale: Per-user LoRA: +1.784 bpb on unrelated text (17/20 users worse); per-user Engram row: +0.00005 bpb (0/20 worse); ~34,000× difference; 3-seed mean ratio ~33,000×.

nodes.label: Recall Without Reasoning Gap
nodes.rationale: Per-user LoRA learns direct recall but struggles with indirect reasoning; on base LM: 85% worse; on instruction-tuned bases: 0-20% worse; base strength controls visibility of damage.

nodes.label: Glass Box Mechanism: Transparent Engram Writes
nodes.rationale: Engram write is observable: gate rises from 0.02 to 0.99 at trigger, stays off elsewhere; residual change cosine 0.999 to value-path projection; maximum non-trigger change exactly 0.000; fails if written to wrong layer.

nodes.label: Additive Composition of Override Maps
nodes.rationale: Override maps with disjoint addresses commute; corporate facts + user facts stack additively at inference without retraining combiner; lossless when domains have disjoint trigger templates.

nodes.label: Knowledge Editing vs User-as-Engram
nodes.rationale: Knowledge editing changes facts model already holds; User-as-Engram adds new facts model never saw; opposite problem with different solutions (locate-and-rewrite vs addressed writes).

nodes.label: User as Engram: Internalizing Per-User Memory as Local Parametric Edits
nodes.rationale: Proposes separating per-user memory into two components: local parametric edits (engram) for facts and shared reasoning skill (LoRA), solving the conflict between remembering and reasoning in adapter-based personalization.

nodes.label: Engram Architecture: Content-Addressable Memory
nodes.rationale: Five-stage mechanistic design: (1) deterministic hash addressing via N-gram triggers, (2) gated value injection (α 0.02→0.99), (3) exact locality (Δ=0.000 at non-trigger positions), (4) late-layer insertion for effective deepening, (5) surface-keyed lookup prevents multi-hop composition.

nodes.label: Local-λ Mix Interaction (LλMI) Block
nodes.rationale: Architectural component that summarizes spatial contexts and global semantic priors into fixed-size linear matrices, enabling efficient self- and cross-attention equivalents while preserving semantic reasoning.

nodes.label: Adaptive Multi-Granularity Distillation Strategy
nodes.rationale: Dynamically balances coarse-grained (16×16), fine-grained (64×64), and perceptual losses via adaptive gradient-based weighting to transfer knowledge from teacher to lightweight student while maintaining latent-space efficiency.

nodes.label: Layered Design: Engram + Shared LoRA
nodes.rationale: Architectural decomposition pairing per-user engram (local facts, 88 KB/user) with shared LoRA (reasoning skill, 11.8 MB global) to eliminate contamination while enabling indirect reasoning without per-user parameter overhead.

nodes.label: LOCOMO: Long-term Conversational Memory Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Evaluation framework measuring both direct single-fact recall and indirect multi-hop reasoning over stored facts, with token-F1 and LLM-judge metrics to assess memory quality and reasoning capability.

nodes.label: PixelHacker: Teacher Model (862M)
nodes.rationale: High-capacity baseline using Latent Categories Guidance (LCG) for semantic priors; serves as teacher for knowledge distillation in Moebius and comparison baseline for User-as-Engram experiments.

nodes.label: Mini-Engram-d8: 178M Parameter Model
nodes.rationale: Smallest experimental variant used for ablations and mechanistic analysis; demonstrates engram mechanism scales from 178M to 1.22B parameters with consistent architectural properties.

nodes.label: Mini-Engram-d12: 339M Parameter Model
nodes.rationale: Mid-scale experimental variant; primary testbed for density curves, insertion strategies, and layered design comparisons.

nodes.label: Mini-Engram-d20: 1.22B Parameter Model
nodes.rationale: Largest experimental variant; demonstrates engram mechanism maintains locality and reasoning separation at scale; used for final layered design and cross-schema generalization studies.

nodes.label: Joint OPT: Multi-Fact Optimization Strategy
nodes.rationale: Gradient-based optimization jointly training all touched rows for a user's fact set; achieves 68% top-1 recall at 100 facts/user vs 38% for per-fact OPT-15, with convergence in 1500–8000 steps.

nodes.label: UNEMBED_P: Closed-Form Insertion Strategy
nodes.rationale: Pseudo-inverse marker initialization pointing value path at gold token's unembedding; cheap (no gradient steps) but weak (6% top-1 recall); serves as baseline for OPT-based strategies.

nodes.label: Knowledge Neurons in Transformers
nodes.rationale: Prior work identifying neurons storing factual knowledge; engram mechanism extends this by localizing facts to hash-addressed rows and separating from reasoning skill.

nodes.label: ROME/MEMIT: Knowledge Editing Methods
nodes.source_location: References: Meng et al. NeurIPS 2022, ICLR 2023
nodes.rationale: Rank-One Model Editing and Mass-Editing Memory in Transformers; engram differs by targeting per-user facts rather than global knowledge updates, with zero cross-user leakage.

nodes.label: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
nodes.source_location: Section 6.4, References: Lewis et al. NeurIPS 2020
nodes.rationale: Baseline method for personalization; engram achieves comparable direct recall with 88 KB/user vs RAG's search index overhead, and superior indirect reasoning via shared LoRA.

nodes.label: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation
nodes.rationale: Per-user LoRA baseline; engram separates memory (local edits) from reasoning (shared LoRA) to eliminate contamination (Δbpb +1.7 vs +0.0005) while enabling indirect reasoning.

nodes.label: Complementary Learning Systems Theory
nodes.source_location: References: McClelland et al. 1995, Kumaran et al. 2016
nodes.rationale: Neuroscience foundation: hippocampus stores sparse local traces (engrams), neocortex learns reasoning; engram architecture mirrors this by separating local facts from shared reasoning skill.

nodes.label: Engram Concept: Richard Semon (1904)
nodes.rationale: Historical origin: Semon coined 'engram' for trace an experience etches into living tissue; paper applies this metaphor to parametric edits, where local sparse traces enable memory without forgetting reasoning.

nodes.label: Engram as Metaphor for Sparse Local Memory
nodes.rationale: Paper frames per-user memory as engram (sparse local trace) paired with shared reasoning (slow cortex learning to use it), mirroring neuroscience: one memory does not erase the next, and personalization stops fighting the model.

hyperedges.label: Per-User LoRA Contamination and Reasoning Gaps
